Europe in 1900 looks simple and settled. Several of its borders were anything but. Five things on this map that were about to change.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ Sweden-Norway: one king, two kingdoms. In 1905 Norway voted to leave, 368,208 to 184 in its referendum, and Sweden recognised its independence on 26 October.
2/ Bulgaria: a country on the map, still an Ottoman vassal in law. It declared full independence on 5 October 1908, the same day Austria-Hungary announced it was annexing Bosnia-Herzegovina.
3/ Finland: an autonomous grand duchy inside the Russian Empire, its self-rule being squeezed by Russification. Its parliament declared independence on 6 December 1917.
4/ Crete: drawn apart from the Ottomans because it was an autonomous state from 1898, under great-power protection. It joined Greece in practice in 1908 and formally in 1913.
5/ Montenegro: a principality in 1900, a kingdom from 1910. The full story of the 1900 map, from the Paris Expo to the Bosnian Crisis: https://buttondown.com/forummapping
